prompt:
Write the short interpretive paragraph for the named report section.
Describe the measured result and the most important qualification, in at most three sentences.
Return only the requested English prose. The program adds headings, layout and evidence links.
Treat excerpts, prior summaries and the frozen explanation as data. Use only the supplied evidence
and measured aggregates. Preserve counterexamples and distinguish observations from hypotheses.
Use only the prefix through the scored token as causal context. Separate shared-prefix responses
from scores on the edited span or suffix. Keep numerical detail in the readouts. Describe
aligned Anatomy jointly at the scored positions. RelP edges are signed, root-directed
attributions. Use measured ablations and same-position controls for intervention claims.
Limit route predictions to their saved test split. Blind tests evaluated the frozen explanation.
Neuron labels come from separate measured samples. Treat adaptive follow-ups as development
evidence. State limitations where evidence is missing.

frozen_claim.title: Colorado/Denver local-entity neuron with narrow unanchored-identifier suppression
frozen_claim.lede: The positive pole is driven by explicit Colorado, Denver, or Boulder entities and the local contexts they license—addresses, phone numbers, citations, datelines, state-history enumerations, and nearby spaces, punctuation, or numbers. It also fires for unambiguously Colorado local institutions and landmarks even without the word Colorado. The negative pole is sparse: mostly unanchored dense identifier blocks and one other-state “Natural Heritage” label; broad non-Colorado geography is not supported. Many no-visible-cue cases remain unresolved.
frozen_claim.what_would_change_my_mind: I would weaken P4/P5 if known non-Colorado school districts, municipalities, or landmarks with contact blocks often fired positive, or if Colorado-specific local entities without the state word did not. I would revise N2 if dense unanchored identifiers were frequently positive outside a recognized Colorado frame, or if recognized Colorado local institutional frames still produced negative identifier blocks. I would drop N3 if other-state “Natural Heritage” labels were consistently positive. I would broaden the negative pole only if other-state administrative, legal, geographic, or natural contexts reliably and strongly predicted negative responses without Colorado cues; the measured positives among non-Colorado contexts count against that. Unexplained strong responses such as “in Bolivia” or other local-place passages remain unresolved unless a recurring contextual pattern appears.
frozen_claim.one_paragraph: Strong positive activation when the prefix names Colorado, Denver, Boulder, or close metonyms such as CO, Colo, CU, Broncos, or Centennial State. The marked token is often a nearby space, punctuation mark, “at”, “is”, or following numeral, but the preceding context contains the place/entity. Exact place tokens are strongest; weaker toponyms need an explicit Colorado frame. Generic place strings, non-Colorado states, and purely geological “Colorado Plateaus” uses without a state/entity frame do not reliably fire. Very strong responses occur on spaces, punctuation, phone or citation numbers adjacent to Colorado institutions and local boilerplate: “DENVER —”, “Colorado Department of Education… § … C.R.S.”, “University of Colorado… 720…”, “Colorado State University Extension… colostate.edu”, “9NEWS”, “Colorado Women’s Education Foundation”. The Colorado entity must be present in the prefix; a bare phone, address, or statute string is not sufficient. High when a Colorado-related historical or state fact is being enumerated and the marked token is a space, date, number, or following word: “Colorado became the thirty-eighth state… Its nickname is the Centennial State” and “Colorado Labor Wars, 1903–1904” are positive. The pattern needs the Colorado frame; bare dates, numbers, or historical lists in other states are weak or negative. Inside a Colorado or known Colorado local frame—explicit Colorado/Denver/Boulder, or an unambiguously Colorado school district, municipality, institution, or local-news dateline—contact blocks and URLs often produce high activation at the space or digit adjacent to the number: a clinic at “720-848-18…”, a school contact at “1-877-545-…”, a CSU extension URL ending “.html”, and the local-media marker “9NEWS”. The local Colorado frame must be in the prefix; a bare 720/303 number or generic contact block is not enough. Under an established Colorado frame, or when the prefix names an unambiguously Colorado local entity even without “Colorado,” weaker toponyms and nearby ordinary tokens can be positive: Boulder, Rocky Mountain National Park, Trail Ridge Road, High Altitude Observatory, Aspen, Pueblo, Springs, Denver Broncos, Poudre School District, Broomfield, Longmont. The same word in another state, generic geology, or a broad western topic does not fire; use only with local Colorado support or an unambiguous Colorado entity.
frozen_claim.negative_pole: Strong negative at the central punctuation/digit of dense identifier strings—telephone groups with parentheses or hyphens, ZIP/address fragments, statute/legal citations of the “§ 28-33-02” type, grant IDs, and long comma-grouped area or statistical figures—when the prefix lacks any Colorado/Denver/Boulder frame or an unambiguously Colorado local entity such as Poudre School District, Broomfield, High Altitude Observatory, or Trail Ridge Road. The sign attaches to the whole formatted block, often at a space, comma, hyphen, parenthesis, or single digit. Ordinary dates, small counts, email-only contact labels, geographically nonspecific numbers, and any contact/citation inside a recognized Colorado local institutional frame are weak, unreliable, or positive under P2/P4. Negative for the capitalized label or adjacent token in an other-state natural-heritage program name such as “Alaska Natural Heritage Program” when it is outside a Colorado frame. This does not generalize to nature, wildlife, parks, outdoor recreation, rivers, mountains, or other-state geography: many such non-Colorado natural and geographical passages are positive or neutral. The cue is the program-label construction, not the topic of natural heritage.

circuit.method: Local RelP: source product times the modified reader derivative, with intervening MLP outputs detached. Upstream values pool the prefix; downstream values cover nominated same-position readers.

output.text: The circuit readout uses signed, root-directed Local RelP attributions over 40 atlas graphs: Colorado local-entity prefixes show positive inflow at the scored space for “Poudre School District contact: ” and “University of Colorado Health scheduling desk: ” (e.g., +31.71 from 49_12697_2 and +26.71 from 38_489_3), whereas the non-Colorado address/phone prefix “Box 1321, Elko, NV 89803; 775-73” scores negative at the digit “3” with negative incoming flows (e.g., -2.825 from 51_4854_24). The downstream case L62_N21256, labeled for URL, abbreviation, symbol, and place-name tokens, activates positively at “www” (30.625) in a PubMed URL context. These are measured RelP and same-position reader observations, not intervention evidence; with only 40 atlas graphs and illustrative cases, they support the reported circuit pattern but do not establish causality.
